topic: amplifier-state-gated, interleaved three-arm test after recalibration
why_gated: an earlier interleaved run showed bypass and cancel_zero - mathematically the same arm - 15 dB apart at the same gain. Both satisfied reference = gain*microphone internally, so the difference was the amplifier's own limiter engaging after a howl. A fixed -20 dBFS tone with the loop open now precedes every trial and the trial is skipped unless the microphone returns within 1.5 dB of the session baseline.

model.note: refitted on the current on-site H (6 segments, mic -18.1 dBFS, delay 124/125)

-6 dB.cancel_zero: held by guard but at the rail: mic -2.7 dBFS, peak 0.0

0 dB.cancel_zero: held by guard but at the rail: mic -1.17 dBFS, peak 0.0

gate_fail_explanation: the -3 dB row failed its gates because the cancel_zero rail event at -6 dB pushed the amplifier into limiting; the next trials then read a lower baseline and were skipped. That is the gate doing its job.
verdict: within one gated session the refitted model keeps the cancel arm stable at 0 dB (mic -35.4 dBFS) while the zero-coefficient arm is already at full scale at -6 dB (mic -2.7 dBFS). Cancellation now buys at least 6 dB of usable gain. The earlier 'cancel howls at -6 dB' result came from the mismatched calibration batch.
caveats: the guard does not trip on microphone clipping, so 'held' must be read together with the microphone level; a rail-level capture is instability, not stability
the -3 dB column has no valid row in this session
amplifier state must be re-gated after any run that reaches the rail
